name: ASD-STE100 Skill
works_with: Claude Code, and other agents through the skills CLI
short: An AI skill that rewrites unclear English into Simplified Technical English, so tool descriptions and errors can't be misread.
what: This skill applies the rules of ASD-STE100, the controlled English the aerospace industry uses so maintenance instructions can't be misread. It flags each sentence that breaks a rule (passive voice, long sentences, several instructions in one, vague words) and rewrites it without dropping any fact or condition. It also ships a linter script that checks the structural rules.
who: People writing text another agent or a non-native reader has to parse with no one to ask: tool descriptions, error messages, system prompts and messages between agents. The author says it's not for creative writing or marketing copy, and it doesn't include the official STE dictionary, so it can't certify compliance.
needs: Python, to run the optional linter

steps.title: Install with the skills CLI
steps.text: Run it from your project root. It installs the skill for the current project.

steps.title: Or clone it for every Claude Code project
steps.text: Best if you want a live copy you update with `git pull`.

steps.title: Ask for a rewrite
steps.text: Paste your text and ask your agent to disambiguate it or apply STE100. You get only the rewritten text back. Add "show the diff" to see which rules it applied.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Rewrite this error message so an agent can't misparse it

watch: The skills CLI sends anonymous install telemetry (skill name and timestamp). Set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` to opt out.
It fixes the form of a text, not its substance. The README says a paragraph with nothing to say comes out short, clean and still empty.
A clean lint result only means the structural checks passed. The linter doesn't compare the rewrite with the original or prove the meaning stayed the same.
